skills.name: Perimeter
skills.description: The total length of the boundary.

PA_AREA_FOR_PERIM.label: Works out the area when asked for the perimeter
PA_AREA_FOR_PERIM.explanation: Multiplies length and width for the distance round.

PA_HALF_PERIM.label: Adds only two sides for the perimeter
PA_HALF_PERIM.explanation: Says a 7 by 3 rectangle has perimeter 10.

PA_PERIM_FOR_AREA.label: Works out the perimeter when asked for the area
PA_PERIM_FOR_AREA.explanation: Adds all four sides for the space inside.

PA_ADD_SIDES.label: Adds length and width to find the area
PA_ADD_SIDES.explanation: Says a 7 by 3 rectangle has area 10.

PA_SUBTRACT_SIDE.label: Subtracts instead of dividing to find a missing side

perimeter.title: Perimeter
perimeter.big_idea: Perimeter is the total length of the edge: imagine walking all the way round the shape. For a rectangle that means adding all four sides, not just two.
steps: Mark each side's length, including the ones not written (opposite sides are equal).
Write the unit: cm, m … (not cm²).
perimeter.sense_check: A fence round a 7 m by 3 m garden needs 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 m of fencing.

worked_examples.prompt: Perimeter of a 7 cm by 3 cm rectangle?
Perimeter of a square with 5 cm sides?

area_rectangles.title: Area of rectangles
area_rectangles.big_idea: Area is how many unit squares fit inside a shape. A 7 cm by 3 cm rectangle holds 3 rows of 7 squares, so its area is 7 × 3 = 21 cm².
steps: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
The answer is in square units: cm², m².
If you know the area and one side, divide to find the other side.
area_rectangles.sense_check: Adding the sides (7 + 3 = 10) measures a length, not the space inside.

worked_examples.prompt: Area of a 7 cm by 3 cm rectangle?
